summary: Shikaripur N. Sridhar works in linguistics and Indology. He has served at Stony Brook University as Chair (attested 2007) and Director of the Center for India Studies (attested 2026).
Shikazo Mori was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Sinology. He studied at Kyoto University from circa 1926 to 1929 and later held a post at Bukkyo University from circa 1970 to 1979.

Shili Xiong was a scholar of philosophy, Buddhist studies, and Sinology who studied at China Inner Studies College under Jian Ouyang in 1920. He held posts at Boone University (~1920–1922), Peking University (1923–1955), and Zhejiang University (~1937–1938).

Shimei Futabatei was a linguist who studied at Senshu College, Tokyo School of Foreign Languages, and Hitotsubashi University. He held positions at the Army War College, Tokyo School of Foreign Languages, Naval War College, Osaka Asahi Shimbun, and Tokyo Asahi Shimbun.

Shin Fujinaga is a scholar of Indology and philosophy. His career includes posts at Hiroshima University (attested 1992) and as an associate professor at the National Institute of Technology, Miyakonojo College (attested 2000).

Shin'ichi Hisamatsu was a Buddhist studies and philosophy scholar who studied at Kyoto University under Kitaro Nishida. His career included professorships at Hanazono University, Ryukoku University, Kyoto University, and Kyoto City University of Arts, alongside visiting at Harvard Divinity School.

Shin'ichi Tsuda is an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo and the Australian National University. He held posts at Toyo Bunko, Toho Gakuin, and the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies.

Shin'ichi Yoshinaga was a religious studies and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Kyoto University. He founded the Kindai Piramiddo Kyokai and served as a professor at the National Institute of Technology, Maizuru College (attested 2015).

Shindai Sekiguchi was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Taisho University from circa 1928 to 1932. He later served as a professor at Taisho University (~1960–1978) and Hanazono University (~1978–1985).

Shindo Kusumoto is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He earned a PhD from Hiroshima University in 2001, where he was supervised by Shoryu Katsura and studied under Hideyo Ogawa, Hiromi Yoshimura, Kazufumi Oki, Osamu Hayashima, and Tomoyuki Uno.

Shingen Takagi was a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar who studied at Tohoku and Rissho universities under Gisho Nakano, Yusho Miyasaka, Ensho Kanakura, and Hakuyu Hadano. He served as an associate professor and later president of Koyasan University.

Shingo Einoo is an Indology and religious studies scholar who earned a PhD at the University of Marburg under Wilhelm Rau. He held posts at the National Museum of Ethnology (~1984–1989) and the University of Tokyo (~1989–2013).

Shinichi Nakazawa is a religious studies, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1969–1977). He held posts at Chuo University (~1993–2006), Tama Art University (~2006–2021), and Meiji University (~2011–2021).

Shinjiro Kazama is a linguist who studied at Hokkaido University (~1984–1993). He held a post at Tottori University from circa 1998 to 2009 and became a professor at Tokyo University of Foreign Studies around 2009.

Shinjo Kawasaki is a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar who studied at Columbia University and under Hajime Nakamura. He held positions at Toyo Bunko, University at Buffalo, University of Tokyo, University of Tsukuba, and Taisho University.

Shinjo Mochizuki was a scholar of Buddhist studies, history, and archaeology. He completed his studies at Kyoto University and the University of Tokyo (~1920–1924) and held a post at Tezukayama Gakuin University circa 1966.

Shinjo Suguro was a Buddhist studies scholar who completed undergraduate and doctoral studies at the University of Tokyo. He served as vice director of the Institute for the Comprehensive Study of Lotus Sutra and was a professor at Rissho University.

Shinkai Sugawara was a scholar in Buddhist and religious studies who studied at Waseda University and earned a doctorate from Taisho University. He served as a professor emeritus at Waseda University, where he held a post from circa 1960 to 1996.

Shinkan Murakami is a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy who completed his doctoral studies at Tohoku University. He served as a professor at Tohoku University (~1978–1996) and later held a post at Seiwa Gakuen College (~1996–2004).

Shinko Mochizuki was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Bukkyo, Taisho, and Tokyo universities. He held academic posts at Waseda University, Chion-in Temple, the Japan Academy, and Taisho University, where he served as professor and president.
